proof:
# A common interior section does not restore projected Grunbaum depth

There are actual convex sources in R times R^2, with arbitrarily many
positive full-dimensional integer fibers and one constant point interior
to EVERY real fiber, whose projected ordinary maximal halfspace depth
is strictly below Gamma_2=4/9. Thus adding a common affine interior
section does not repair the projected-Gamma shortcut. No failure of the
mixed target Gamma_2/2 is asserted. An explicit all-oblique mixed center
below separately verifies that target when the number of large fibers
is odd, including the smallest displayed choice N=3.

## 1. Exact source and common interior section

Let T=conv(0,e_1,e_2), V=|T|=1/2, b=1/3, c=2/3, and g=(b,b).
Choose an integer N>=3 and 0<epsilon<=1/100. Put

    E=conv(0,g+epsilon e_1,g+epsilon e_2),
    e=|E|/V=epsilon(c+epsilon),
    theta=e/(4N), p=(b-theta,b-theta).

The two nonzero vertices of E have nonnegative coordinates and sum
c+epsilon<1; thus E subset T. The determinant of its vertex matrix
[[b+epsilon,b],[b,b+epsilon]] is epsilon(c+epsilon), proving its volume.
Let

    C=conv(([0,N-1] times T) union ({N} times E)).

This is a full-dimensional compact convex body. Its integer fibers
are exactly N copies of T at 0,...,N-1 and E at N, with no others.
For z<=N-1 the product already gives T and all generators lie in T
in continuous coordinates. At z=N exposedness forces the fiber E.
For N-1<=z<=N the fiber is (N-z)T+(z-N+1)E. In particular every real
fiber above [0,N] contains E.

In the barycentric coordinates of E, p has the two non-apex weights

    (b-theta)/(c+epsilon), (b-theta)/(c+epsilon).

They are positive and have sum (c-2theta)/(c+epsilon)<1. Hence p is
interior to E and to every real fiber, including the endpoint fibers.
The mixed mass is (N+e)V; no single fiber carries half that mass.

The exact continuous projection of the mixed measure has density

    rho=N 1_T+1_E.

No integral over the base or continuous width replaces this integer sum.

## 2. A simultaneous three-cap upper certificate

Write lambda_0=1-x_1-x_2, lambda_1=x_1, lambda_2=x_2 and take

    H_0={lambda_0>=b+2theta},
    H_i={lambda_i>=b-theta}, i=1,2.

All three boundaries pass through p. The three thresholds sum to one,
so these halfspaces cover ALL R^2: if a point were strictly below all
three thresholds, its barycentric coordinate sum would be less than one.
Thus an upper bound for each of their masses is an upper bound for
ordinary maximal depth at every continuous point, without requiring the
point to equal p. Their cylindrical lifts are genuine ambient halfspaces.

Their exact masses divided by V are

    B_0=N(c-2theta)^2+e[(c-2theta)/(c+epsilon)]^2,
    B_i=N(c+theta)^2
          +e[1-(b-theta)^2/(b(b+epsilon))], i=1,2.       (1)

For H_0, its E trace is the apex homothety of ratio
(c-2theta)/(c+epsilon). For H_i, its complement in E is the apex
triangle cut at level b-theta. On the two apex edges the ratios are
(b-theta)/(b+epsilon) and (b-theta)/b, giving the complement fraction
in (1). All cuts are proper; their boundaries have zero planar volume.

Let Gamma=4/9. Since the E contribution to B_0 is at most e, expanding
its large-triangle contribution and using 4Ntheta=e gives

    B_0<=N Gamma+e(1/3+theta).                           (2)

For the other E fraction, direct subtraction gives

    1-(b-theta)^2/(b(b+epsilon))
       =(b epsilon+2b theta-theta^2)/(b(b+epsilon))
       <=3epsilon+6theta.

Expansion of N(c+theta)^2 therefore gives

    B_i<=N Gamma+e(1/3+3epsilon+25theta/4).              (3)

The bounds N>=3 and epsilon<=1/100 imply

    theta=epsilon(c+epsilon)/(4N)<=epsilon/16,

since c+epsilon<3/4. Consequently (2)-(3) give, for every i,

    B_i <= N Gamma+e(1/3+217/6400)
         = Gamma(N+e)-(4447/57600)e.                   (4)

The last coefficient is positive. Thus the ordinary projected maximum
D(rho), normalized by the total projected mass, satisfies

    D(rho) <= Gamma-(4447/57600)e/(N+e) < Gamma.         (5)

This exact finite upper cover has its common meeting point INTERIOR to
every source fiber. Translating all continuous coordinates by -p also
gives the same counterexample with the common interior section zero.
The integer lattice, all ambient halfspaces and all fiber volumes are
preserved by that translation.

## 3. The ordinary and mixed lower bounds are separate

The retained N copies of T in the projected law show

    D(rho)>=N Gamma/(N+e)>Gamma/2

at g, using ordinary Grunbaum for T in each direction. This only proves
an ordinary projected lower bound and is not used as an oblique mixed
depth guarantee.

For a separate actual mixed center, take N=2k+1 odd, k>=1, and y=(k,g).
For an arbitrary ambient halfspace through y, write its margin as

    alpha(z-k)+u.(x-g)>=0.

If u is nonzero, at each of the at least k+1 large-fiber bases with
alpha(z-k)>=0, its trace contains the ordinary through-g cap of T.
Those fibers contribute at least (k+1)Gamma V. If u=0, the same
bases contribute their full V each, which is no smaller. Every containing
halfspace includes its parallel through-y halfspace, so all such
halfspaces have normalized mass at least

    Gamma(k+1)/(N+e)>Gamma/2,

where strictness uses e<1 and 2(k+1)=N+1. This proof retains the one
common oblique normal and includes vertical caps with boundary mass.
Hence N=3, and every odd N in the family, separately satisfies OC.

## 4. Scope

The result obstructs the ordinary Gamma theorem for projected counting
laws even under a common affine interior section. It neither determines
the exact projected maximum nor supplies a general mixed source theorem.
Its proof does not infer any depth lower bound from its cap-cover upper
bound. The verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_common_interior_projected_count_obstruction.py`
checks exact cap formulas, membership, and all rational budget gaps.
